title: Cell Structure: The Fundamental Unit of Life
summary: Understand prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, the plasma membrane and major organelles.
body:
Every living organism is made up of one or more cells. The cell is the structural and functional unit of life.

Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus, while eukaryotic cells possess a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

The plasma membrane is selectively permeable. Mitochondria are involved in aerobic respiration, chloroplasts in photosynthesis, and ribosomes in protein synthesis.

Study tip: Draw and label a plant cell and an animal cell and compare their structural features.

title: Light Reaction of Photosynthesis — Quick Notes
summary: Discover Photosystem 2, the electron transport chain, ATP and NADPH formation.
body:
The light reaction takes place on the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts. Light energy excites electrons in the photosystems.

Photosystem 2 absorbs light and replaces lost electrons using electrons from water splitting, which releases oxygen and protons.

Electron transport builds a proton gradient that powers ATP synthase. Photosystem 1 energizes electrons again; NADP+ is reduced to NADPH.

ATP and NADPH support carbon fixation in the Calvin cycle. These are introductory notes: check the NCERT chapter for all details.

title: Mendelian Genetics: Laws of Inheritance
summary: A beginner-friendly overview of dominance, segregation and independent assortment.
body:
Gregor Mendel studied inheritance using pea plants. His experiments led to key principles explaining how traits pass between generations.

The law of segregation states that the two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation.

The law of independent assortment describes the independent distribution of alleles of different genes when genes are unlinked. Linked genes may not assort independently.

Practice with monohybrid and dihybrid crosses to build confidence.
